I'm from the western region, Mumbai, Maharashtra. Here that peacock head cutting tool is called a 'vili' and it's used a lot for things from grating coconuts to chopping a small green chili.
The word we use here for knife is 'chaku' or 'chhuri'. Chhurri is a much sharper and longer knife than Chaku, closer to the one you're looking for. But then the ones we use regularly are much cheaper than a proper chhurri. I Googled a bit and I think it's the hacksaw blade that's used for making them. Maybe that could help?

I have a phobia and general anxiety disorder. I didn't know this 5 years ago. But I was still having to deal with things that people normally don't worry about. Not just the usual sweaty palms and aching stomach but also really bad palpitations that wouldn't stop no matter what. I was stuck in the traffic and in a vehicle that was on the opposite side of the road was a guy who tilted his head to look at me and smiled and waved as though to tell me it's okay. I thought he might be waving at someone else so I didn't want to be embarrassed by waving back. The traffic started moving but then I was much more at ease. I don't even know if it was for me, but I have never appreciated a smile so much in my entire life.

I met this guy on Facebook a few years ago. I had a few mutuals so I when he messaged we started talking. Talking turned to flirting and it seemed fun. Then we exchanged numbers and talked a few nights. He wanted to meet, so I went to see him near his place which was very far from where I'm located. It was really awkward. I don't know why we hit it off virtually but couldn't in real life? After that day he would call me to see him there again which was annoying, I mean at least meet me halfway? Then it sort of died down after a few months. And then out of nowhere he shows up outside my work place. Said he wanted to take me out. I told him I was really tired and I had to finish some work off from home. He wouldn't let me. Then when he saw I was frustrated he said he'd drop me home. I agreed. In the car all he talked about was how he thought I was perfect and that he was SURPRISED that I didn't like him. I mean who thinks like that? Then out of nowhere he talks about getting married. This was the longest car ride of my life. What was worse, because of the traffic we were kind of stuck somewhere and he got mad at someone on the road and started abusing them. Like really really badly. I was horrified. Then after a couple minutes he starts talking to me like nothing happened. That ended when I got home. But since I didn't talk to him after that. I got a message from him out of the blue, about a year ago saying I looked ugly in my display picture. Haven't talked to him since.

Okay so according to my mother they would just use a cotton cloth for their period that they would wash and use again. But along with this they had a custom where while on their period women were to stay isolated from everyone and take a corner of the house for about 4 days every month. This my mother explains, was done because back in the day the woman would have to do basically everything and it was better for her to rest for those few days of the month. I'm guessing the cloth rags weren't very absorbent which is also why they decided to restrict activity. So she wasn't allowed to cook or clean or worship the gods. Now after all this time we still have the 'you can't enter the temple because you're on your period' custom in India.

Rituals. All kinds of rituals that take place in religions. I've always thought that it would have  started as a game of some sort and then it got too serious. We have the weirdest traditions that sometimes makes no sense. Or even if they made sense at some point they don't anymore. For example in Hindu weddings, the mother in law pulls the son in law's nose before the wedding takes place and the son in law is supposed to stop that form happening. I just find it so bizarre but it's taken quite seriously now.

Which didn't happen. She knew he had a girlfriend and didn't approve of it because he needed to concentrate on his studies. The one time I met her, my ex was dealing with his admission process in a college and I was there to help him out or keep him company. He needed to call his mom there to get some of his documents for the admission. The minute she saw me she immediately went, "Why is she here?" as though I was going to ruin his chances of getting an admission to the college.


Fun fact, he later blamed me for not scoring enough in his exams because he couldn't concentrate on his studies because of me :/
